title: Erdos #993 depth-3 proof frontier
scope: The remaining depth-3 log-concavity rung in the matching-bag approach; this graph is not a proof of full tree independence-sequence unimodality.

claims.slogan: The remaining alpha 17--19, deficiency at most five rung has no depth-3 log-concavity break.
claims.statement: For every tree T with alpha(T) in {17,18,19} and matching deficiency delta=2 alpha(T)-|V(T)| at most 5, if s_d=i_{alpha-d}(T), then s_3^2 >= s_2 s_4.
claims.scope: Trees in the final enumeration-reachable depth-3 window only.
claims.falsification: One exact tree in the stated window with s_3^2 < s_2 s_4 refutes the claim.

direct: near-maximum independent sets of a tree log-concave at defect three
obstruction: tree independent sets three below maximum violate a Turan inequality

claims.slogan: A maximum matching turns a tree independence polynomial into a port-labeled bag CSP with alpha bags.
claims.statement: Contracting the edges of a maximum matching M in a tree T gives alpha(T) one- or two-vertex bags, and independent sets of T are in weight-preserving bijection with feasible bag assignments.
claims.scope: Every finite forest, hence every finite tree.
claims.falsification: A finite forest for which the bag construction fails to partition vertices or fails to preserve feasible-assignment weights refutes the claim.

claims.slogan: Maximum assignments form an order-ideal code of a forest-cover poset, times constant coordinates.
claims.statement: After complementing maximum independent sets to minimum vertex covers and gauging the matching-edge variables, the free assignments are the order ideals of a poset with forest cover graph; forced bags contribute constant coordinates.
claims.scope: Every finite forest equipped with a maximum matching.
claims.falsification: A finite forest whose maximum-assignment code is not equivalent to the stated order-ideal code refutes the claim.

claims.slogan: The extendable erasure profile is log-concave with an explicit depth-3 Pascal reserve.
claims.statement: For M>=4, the extendable profile satisfies 27(M-3)e_3^2 >= 32(M-2)e_2e_4, hence e_3^2-e_2e_4 >= 0.
claims.scope: Every downward-closed family after the Pascal transform; transported to every finite tree maximum-assignment code.
claims.falsification: A downward-closed family or transported tree code violating the displayed integer inequality refutes the claim.

claims.slogan: Every minimal blocked residual through defect four is an alternating comparison path.
claims.statement: For an erased bag set D with |D|<=4, every minimal unsatisfiable residual component is a path on erased bags whose endpoint forces collide; in the poset gauge it is a violated transitive comparison along the unique cover path.
claims.scope: Maximum-matching bag CSPs of trees, at defect at most four.
claims.falsification: A minimal blocked residual with at most four erased bags that is not a forced path refutes the classification.

claims.slogan: Near-maximum independent sets split into extendable and blocked partial assignments.
claims.statement: For each defect d, s_d=i_{alpha-d}(T)=e_d+b_d, where e_d counts bag assignments extendable to a maximum assignment and b_d counts the remaining feasible assignments.
claims.scope: Every finite tree and every defect.
claims.falsification: Any tree, matching choice, and defect for which the two classes overlap, omit an assignment, or give the wrong coefficient refutes the identity.

claims.slogan: The corrected Turan margin is the extendable reserve plus blocked reserve plus a mixed cross term.
claims.scope: All nonnegative sequences satisfying s=e+b; no tree hypothesis is needed.
claims.falsification: One exact integer substitution satisfying s=e+b but violating the identity refutes the claim.

claims.slogan: The proposed blocked-profile log-concavity lemma is false in the target rung.
claims.statement: For the matching-bag decomposition of every tree in the target scope, b_3^2 >= b_2 b_4.
claims.scope: Refuted at (n,alpha,deficiency)=(33,19,5): one exact lift has (b_2,b_3,b_4)=(1,16,4216), hence b_3^2-b_2b_4=-3960.
claims.falsification: One tree and maximum-matching bag decomposition with b_3^2 < b_2 b_4 refutes the claim.

direct: independent sets not contained in any maximum independent set counted by size
obstruction: rank sequence of faces not contained in a maximum-dimensional facet
minimal obstruction certificates imply log-concavity of nonextendable partial assignments
generating_function: generating polynomial for feasible partial assignments that do not extend to an optimal solution
csp_sat: minimally unsatisfiable tree CSPs counted by number of unassigned variables
simplicial_complex: rank sequence of the nonpure part of a simplicial independence complex

claims.slogan: The extendable Pascal reserve absorbs the adverse mixed blocked/extendable cross term.
claims.statement: For the matching-bag decomposition of every tree in the target scope, (e_3^2-e_2e_4)+(2e_3b_3-e_2b_4-e_4b_2) >= 0.
claims.scope: Exact evidence covers every nonisomorphic tree through n=18 and 500 targeted lifts in the (n,alpha,deficiency)=(33,19,5) cell, including 57 with a negative mixed term; the intended theorem scope is the remaining alpha 17--19 rung.
claims.falsification: One tree and maximum-matching bag decomposition with the displayed cross-reserve margin negative refutes the claim.

direct: log-concavity preserved when a correction sequence is partially synchronized with a sequence having quantitative Turan slack
probabilistic_event: quantitative second-order union bound for overlapping path obstruction events on a forest
matching_poset: charge violated transitive comparisons in a forest poset to order-preserving partial assignments
obstruction: negative mixed Turan cross term bounded by a base log-concavity reserve

claims.slogan: The Pascal reserve must absorb the mixed and blocked-profile deficits jointly.
claims.statement: For every tree in the target scope, ((5 alpha+17)/(27(alpha-3)))e_2e_4+(b_3^2-b_2b_4)+(2e_3b_3-e_2b_4-e_4b_2) >= 0; together with the proved Pascal reserve and the depth-3 decomposition, this implies s_3^2-s_2s_4>=0.
claims.scope: The remaining alpha 17--19, deficiency at most five rung; targeted evidence covers 500 lifts in the (33,19,5) cell, including 57 with adverse combined correction.
claims.falsification: One target-scope tree whose displayed Pascal lower margin is negative refutes this sufficient bridge; a negative full margin would also refute the depth-3 rung itself.

edges.note: The Lean forest-poset project formalizes both layers; this non-dependency edge records the formal interface.

bridges.title: Ordered cover deletion and a canonical first violated comparison
bridges.source_theory: P-partitions and ordered deletion of poset cover relations
bridges.shared_object: A forest poset together with a weakening of its transitive comparison constraints.
bridges.translation: Fix an order on the transitive comparisons missing from the retained cover-path CSP and assign each blocked partial assignment to its first violated comparison. This would disjointify the union of obstruction-path events.
missing_hypotheses: The first-violation classes must admit exact defect-refined counts.
The ordered deletion must respect the erased-path interpretation rather than only the abstract relation set.
The resulting class formulas must yield a joint blocked-plus-cross reserve inequality.
bridges.expected_payoff: Replace overlap inclusion-exclusion by a disjoint partition of b_2,b_3,b_4 and expose path-local summands that can be charged to the Pascal reserve.
bridges.kill_test: Enumerate the canonical first-violation classes on every tree through n=15 and check that their disjoint counts reproduce b_2,b_3,b_4 exactly before proving any inequality.
bridges.falsification: A blocked assignment with no unique first violated comparison under the frozen rule, or a mismatch between the class sum and b_d, kills the proposed translation.

evidence.note: TheoremGraph surfaced Lemmas 4.4 and 4.6; they motivate ordered deletion but do not prove the local counting claim.

bridges.title: Minimally unsatisfiable tree CSPs and implication paths
bridges.shared_object: A minimal unsatisfiable residual whose implication graph is a path between conflicting endpoint forces.
bridges.translation: Encode each erased matched bag as a Boolean variable and each port constraint as a binary clause; minimal blocked residuals become path-shaped minimally unsatisfiable formulas.
missing_hypotheses: Known minimal-unsatisfiability structure theorems do not count residuals by defect.
The clause encoding must preserve multiplicity of surrounding occupied assignments.
No retrieved theorem currently supplies log-concavity or the needed quantitative count.
bridges.expected_payoff: Potentially provide a canonical certificate language or tree recurrence for the joint blocked-plus-cross correction, but the current path classification already captures most of the structural content.
bridges.kill_test: Compare SAT-certificate classes with the existing alternating-path classes on all residual CSPs through four erased bags; abandon the bridge if it adds no sharper count or recurrence.
bridges.falsification: Failure of the Boolean encoding to preserve minimality or assignment multiplicity, or absence of a new quantitative lemma, removes this bridge from the active queue.

bridges.title: Nonextendable faces in a nonpure independence complex
bridges.source_theory: Simplicial complexes, pure skeleta, and face-number inequalities
bridges.shared_object: b_d counts independent faces of size alpha-d that are not contained in any alpha-face.
bridges.translation: View the extendable faces as the pure alpha-generated subcomplex and b_d as the rank sequence of its complement inside the tree independence complex.
missing_hypotheses: The complement of the pure-generated subcomplex is not itself a simplicial complex.
No retrieved theorem gives log-concavity of this nonextendable rank profile.
Any algebraic invariant must retain the forest-poset path geometry.
bridges.expected_payoff: This proposed route would have proved blocked-profile log-concavity, but that target is false in the intended rung.
bridges.kill_test: Search for an exact theorem on the rank sequence of faces outside maximum facets; then test its hypotheses on the known tree complexes and small arbitrary complexes before adaptation.
bridges.falsification: A small tree whose blocked profile violates the proposed imported inequality, or a theorem whose domain excludes the nonpure complement, kills the bridge.

bridges.title: Dependency-graph bounds for overlapping path-obstruction events
bridges.source_theory: Bonferroni, Hunter, Janson, and dependency-graph inequalities
bridges.shared_object: b_d is the measure of a union of local path-obstruction events under the uniform counting measure on defect-d feasible assignments.
bridges.translation: Treat each violated comparison path as an event and use the intersection graph of path events to control overlap terms in the union count.
missing_hypotheses: The assignment measure is conditioned on feasibility and fixed defect, so standard independence assumptions may fail.
The path-event intersection graph need not be a forest.
A probability bound must be sharp enough to fit inside the explicit Pascal reserve.
bridges.expected_payoff: Could bound overlap without exact inclusion-exclusion if local pair intersections dominate the adverse cross term.
bridges.kill_test: Compute the best available first- and second-order union bounds for every n<=15 instance and compare their slack with the exact cross-reserve margin.
bridges.falsification: If the sharp tested dependency-graph bound exceeds the reserve on a small tree, close this bridge unless a stronger tree-specific inequality is identified.

evidence.note: TheoremGraph surfaced a Hunter-type tree Bonferroni lemma; applicability here is unproved.
